files.summary: Offline execution, sync and distributed locks. Covers local-first principles P1-P8; the op model (op kinds, base versions or subtree digest, UUIDv7 ids and deriveIno for copies); the outbox record, its states and ordering (cseq plus a Lamport counter, no HLC, server-clamped mtime); an ordered op lane and a control lane. The syncd connection state machine is a Mermaid diagram with full-jitter back-off (0.5 s base, 30 s cap), a 25 s dead-man timer, the offline probe and NetStatus mapping. OS sessions are one per kernel instance and login; supersession uses deviceId and kernelEpoch (close 4409), and a newer session releases a crashed predecessor's leases. Resume goes through the per-owner feed (feed_seq and feed_purged_seq horizon), with an ordered broadcaster, a buffered stream-to-live switch, permission-filtered and redacted entries, and a paged snapshot with version-guarded apply. Replay uses op.batch (at most 32 ops per frame) with a credit window of 16; the limiter throttles and never disconnects; a retry resets the lane head. The server pipeline table records which outcomes op_log persists and which are transient. Includes an exactly-once proof sketch; conflicted copies and salvage to ~/lost+found; parked local copies and the rejection cascade; synchronous commit (SYNC_WAIT_MS = 10 s) and cancel through proc.signal. Leases are S/X with TTL 30 s (15 s in the demo), heartbeat at TTL/3, fencing, a heap-based sweeper, crash expiry at most TTL + 0.5 s, hidden-tab re-verification and read-only mode for the second writer. Also covers the offline utility matrix, taskbar status and degraded list (OFF-04), and the Service Worker versioned precache with SKIP_WAITING on reboot (OFF-05). Section 4 has the envelope, three JSON Schemas (common, client-to-server, server-to-client; validated), field tables, close codes, constants and backpressure. The test plan includes the exactly-once property test (dropped acks, duplicated frames, server kill after COMMIT), the 5,000-op replay, the hidden-tab lease test and crash expiry.

Backend API and server runtime. One Node 24 process with Fastify plugins: a topology diagram, module tree, plugin dependency graph and owner table. Includes the request lifecycle and hook order, the configuration table (no default secrets; production guards, exit 78), and an error model with a status-to-errno table. Every endpoint is listed with method, path, auth, rate class, body limit, success and errors: auth (login, logout, me, su, su revoke, guest, password), /ws, sync snapshot, ops/{opId}, blobs PUT/GET/HEAD (HEAD answers only for readable content), swap PUT/GET/list/DELETE, index put/pull/search/verify, llm plan/extract/answer/health, telemetry consent/upload/download/delete, /api/debug/fault (root, FAULT_INJECTION=1, OS-session scoped, one-shot), admin probes, healthz, readyz, and internal metrics. Covers WS upgrade authentication (Origin allowlist and cookie before the upgrade; 4 sockets per session). The session model covers auth_sessions, os_sessions and the su grant, with an ER diagram; tokens and cookies; validation; revocation within 1 s (close 4401 and lease release); Argon2id with a semaphore of 2. The token-bucket limiter uses keys bounded by dsa/lru, with a class table. FsBlobStore covers layout, streaming SHA-256, atomic rename, GC (1 h and 14 days) and the advisory-lock fix for the PUT/GC race. The swap API authorises by owner only. The index API has the top-down readable-set CTE and an upward verify CTE that handles hard links. The LLM gateway section covers the pipeline, reserve/settle over database.md pools, a price table checked against the Claude API reference, llm_requests logging, the provider call (Opus 5.5 at effort medium, strict tools, tool_choice auto, refusal fallbacks, prompt caching), cassettes with scrubbing, the temperature-0 rule, degradation and optional upstream forwarding. Also: telemetry opt-in, the fault harness, observability (log fields and redaction, metrics list, healthz/readyz), graceful shutdown with close 1012, and startup self-tests (Argon2id RFC 9106 vector reproduced locally, SHA-256 vector, blob-store probe, DB checks) with first-start credentials. Ends with shapes, invariants, edge cases, budgets and a test plan.

Security model, the normative source for SECURITY.md. Objectives, assumptions and non-goals; assets A-1…A-12; adversaries ADV-1…ADV-11. The threat model has T-01…T-35, each with mitigations and a verifying test. Trust boundaries TB1…TB9 are a Mermaid diagram plus a table. The permission model covers the uid/gid ranges (root, users, bench and demo seed notes, online guests 60000-60999, offline guest 65534), the isomorphic perm.ts with the root x-bit fix, enforcement points, su grants through the secure prompt, the agent identity (drops to the real login uid), and the examiner, demo and guest ring-fencing. Auth and session properties; the offline PBKDF2-600k verifier (never for root, 30-day expiry, password_version invalidation) and a stolen-laptop table. The header table and CSP: C10's directives verbatim plus build-time inline hashes and form-action 'none'; Trusted Types report-only; the CSSOM note. Client isolation on a shared device (shadowing, lint, chunk scan, the recorded about:blank residual risk, first-party code only, secure context, localhost-only local stack). The secrets inventory and rules; the leaked-key runbook with time targets and the incident log (section 18). The agent and RAG trust-boundary summary maps each section 3.4 principle to a mechanism. Also covers the data-at-rest statement, supply chain (pins, digests, blocked install scripts, pinned actions, runner restrictions, licence scan, THIRD_PARTY.md), audit and privacy, admin surfaces, and a security test list: canary password, CSRF and cross-origin WS, fixation, revocation under 1 s, the SYS-01 bypass suites, rag-leak, INJ-20, destructive confirmation, privilege tests, headers, secrets and grants.

cross_spec_requests: database.md: classify op_log outcomes by errno AND reason (§3.9.3 currently treats every EAGAIN, EBUSY and ECANCELED as transient). Persist ECANCELED 'killed', EAGAIN 'stale-version'/'stale-plan' and EBUSY 'lease'/'subtree-busy' on structural ops, so a killed op cannot be re-applied on resend and one long-held lease cannot stall a session's op lane. Keep EBUSY 'lock-timeout', EAGAIN 'retry-exhausted'/'blob-missing', ETIMEDOUT and EIO 'server' transient (offline-and-sync.md §3.10).

database.md: add locks.lease_id uuid UNIQUE (the ABI's leaseId); os_sessions.device_id and kernel_epoch; users.password_version, users.disabled_at, users.telemetry_opt_in_at; the llm_usage 'demo' pool (guests and the public demo account); llm_requests.provider_request_id and refusal_category, purpose 'extract', status 'replayed'.

database.md: add blobKey(sha256) for pg_advisory_xact_lock, held by PUT /api/blobs and by the blob GC around existence check, rename or unlink, and row change. The GC unlinks inside its transaction, and an op that raises refcount from 0 stats the file first. This refines §3.19, which deletes files after COMMIT and leaves a PUT/GC race.

database.md: keep reason and ownerSeqs inside op_log.result. In lockPlan(), affected owners are the owners of every changed inode plus the owners of every directory whose entry set changed. Salvage copies for rejected content ops (EACCES, EPERM, parent ENOENT) go in the rejection transaction with feed rows. Conflicted and salvaged copies get the id deriveIno(opId, ino).

database.md: the demo seed must create alice and bob in group team (gid 200) and examiner accounts in a new 'examiners' group, with fixed uids outside the bench seed's 1001-1059 block; groups guests (60000) and nogroup (65534); confirm may_r/may_x serve snapshot visibility and the per-link verify query.

syscall-abi.md: register detail.reason values blob-missing, predecessor-retry and lease-limit (EAGAIN); principal and csrf (EACCES); guest and opt-in (EPERM); expired (EAIUNAVAIL); checksum on 422. Register the security audit event names (security-model.md §4.3). State that the JSON body's errno overrides the HTTP-status fallback of §4.9. Align ai.index.put to require w on the file (the RAG test and research data flow), not r. Confirm waitingOn = 'sync:result' (architecture.md uses 'net:op:<opId>').

architecture.md: rename the server reply 'welcome' to 'hello.ok' and 'welcome.owners' to 'hello.ok.owners'; the sync spec's catalogue is normative. Add contentWindow, contentDocument and window.open to the chunk-scan ban list (the residual about:blank risk and the first-party-only rule are recorded in security-model.md §3.10).

agentic-shell.md: use sig 'SIGTERM' (ABI SignalName), not 'TERM', in proc.signal; use the registered reason 'no-key', not 'nokey'. debug.delay is sent as POST /api/debug/fault {op:'batch', target:'server', delayMs}. Batch audit rows travel in OpSubmit.audit.records.

virtual-file-system.md: use deriveIno(opId, ino) for recursive copies and for conflicted and salvaged copies; implement the rejection cascade and the 'parked' held state (offline-and-sync.md §3.12.4); key the outbox by [osSessionId, cseq]; export the isomorphic vfs/digest.ts; only session.layout outbox records are coalesced. X-SEC-1 is answered in security-model.md.

memory-and-paging.md and window-manager.md: define WindowLayout for the session.layout op (with rev), including the old (osSessionId, pid, pageIds) per window for MEM-04, at most 32 KiB serialised. The pager uploads swap with X-Plotinium-Checksum (uncompressed SHA-256), Raw-Size and Encoding headers, and keeps a page local-only on 413 EDQUOT.

rag-semantic-search.md: backend-api.md mounts the §4.4 routes as specified. Verify is per link path, handling hard links, and returns the current path. index.put requires w on the file and chunk text equal to the blob slice.
predictive-prefetch.md: define TelemetryEvent (UUIDv7 eventId, appId, kind, ts, context) and the Settings → Privacy flow that calls PUT /api/telemetry/consent; opting out deletes the server copy.

boot-and-services.md and ui-design-system.md: sync and lockd start() do no network I/O, and the first connection happens after desktop-interactive; the update service owns the update.available degraded entry; bootlog records version changes after an update reboot. The inlined boot UI must satisfy the CSP: inline script and style hashed at build time, or loaded as same-origin files, and no inline style attributes. POST shows a non-secure-context diagnostic. The greeter lists only users known on the device, plus Other user and Guest.

deployment-and-ci.md: publish Caddy only on 127.0.0.1:${PLOTINIUM_PORT:-4717} locally; generate CSP inline hashes at build time into the Caddyfile and set the header table of security-model.md §4.1. Cache-Control: no-cache for sw.js, index.html, version.json and the manifest; immutable for hashed assets, and for /models and /ort only under versioned paths. LEASE_TTL_MS=15000 in the demo profile; FAULT_INJECTION=1 only in local compose and 0 in compose.prod.yaml. Use a fixed compose network matching TRUST_PROXY_CIDRS; a DB password generated at first start into a secrets volume (DATABASE_PASSWORD_FILE); ANTHROPIC_API_KEY_FILE with mode 0600 on the VPS. Set stop_grace_period 15s, exactly one app replica, and a healthcheck on /api/readyz. CI: pin actions by commit SHA with least-privilege permissions; restrict the self-hosted runner to schedule and workflow_dispatch on main; add the gitleaks jobs (PR, nightly full history, dist, cassettes) and a licence scan against THIRD_PARTY.md; script the OFF-05 hash-only patch release.

testing-and-performance.md: add the section 7 budgets of all three specs to budgets.json (lock grant ≤ 50 ms server-side, crash expiry ≤ TTL + 0.5 s, revocation < 1 s, verify ≤ 100 ms, event-loop p99 ≤ 20 ms, and others). Run the 6-minute hidden-tab lease test nightly on the lab-spec runner. Include the security test list in TESTING.md, with the canary inspection and the CSP-violation check in e2e. The k6 profile raises limiter capacities through configuration only.
requirements-traceability.md: register the Plotinium ID prefixes SYN-, SRV- and SEC- for tools/traceability.ts.
open_questions: Are dedicated-worker timers exempt from Chrome's intensive throttling on the lab machine? The coherence file marks this UNVERIFIED. The W3 test with a tab hidden for 6 minutes decides; if it fails, which lease TTL will the instructor accept for VFS-09?
Will the instructor accept a hash-only patch tag (for example v1.0.1 with no feature change) deployed during Demo Day to show OFF-05 after the freeze?

Where do the two-user lock demo and the hidden AI prompts run: the examiner's local stack or the production URL? The W3 campus WebSocket test (more than 1 failure in 20 triggers the SSE+POST adapter) is decision-critical.

Credit window: C6 names both 32 and 16. The specs read 16 as ops in flight and 32 as the per-frame schema limit. Confirm, or raise the window if the 5,000-op replay from campus is too slow (estimated about 50 s at 150 ms RTT).
The WebSocket frame bucket (50 frames/s, burst 200) and the other rate-limit values are starting points that must be justified from the W10 measurements; OWASP's example is far lower.
Is the database-restore 'reset' path, which copies local rows newer than a restored server into ~/lost+found/restore-<date>/, required for v1, or is the nightly-backup RPO documented as a limitation?

Outcome classification: database.md §3.9.3 and offline-and-sync.md §3.10 currently disagree on which EAGAIN, EBUSY and ECANCELED outcomes are persisted. R2 and R5 must settle it before the sync engine is built (W6-W9).
Temperature 0 (§12.6): will the instructor accept cassettes, fixed seeds, a frozen clock and three live runs in writing before W4? If not, claude-sonnet-4-6 (accepts temperature) joins the bake-off.
How many named examiner accounts are needed? Should the public demo account have any LLM budget at the final defence? Is handing examiners paper credentials at each gate acceptable?
May the team move to Node 26 LTS (2026-10-28) before v0.2.0 if the CI matrix is green?
Should the repository be public (which affects gitleaks on full history and runner minutes) or private?
Should nightly backups be encrypted client-side with an rclone crypt remote (a new secret kept on paper), or is R2's at-rest encryption enough?
Trusted Types stays report-only because Solid's templates use innerHTML. Confirm this is acceptable. Passkeys (WebAuthn) remain a Phase-4 stretch goal.
